review.tagline: Python and .NET framework for multi-agent apps, now in maintenance mode
review.summary: AutoGen is a layered framework for building multi-agent applications: a Core API for event-driven message passing, an AgentChat API for two-agent and group-chat patterns, and an Extensions API for model clients, MCP tools and code execution. It also ships AutoGen Studio, a no-code prototyping UI on port 8080, and AgentBench. The project is in maintenance mode and community managed; Microsoft points new users to Microsoft Agent Framework.
review.audience: Developers with existing AutoGen code or prototyping multi-agent apps in Python
strengths: Layered design: Core, AgentChat and Extensions APIs let you pick the abstraction level
Core runtime supports local and distributed execution, with Python and .NET packages
MCP tool support through McpWorkbench, e.g. the Playwright MCP server
Includes AutoGen Studio for no-code prototyping and a benchmarking suite
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: no new features, only bug fixes, security patches and docs
Maintainers recommend Microsoft Agent Framework for new projects
AutoGen Studio is explicitly not production-ready and has no built-in authentication
Support is community-only and response times may be slow
needs: Needs Python 3.10+, OpenAI API key (for the quickstart samples), Node.js/npx (for the Playwright MCP example)
